name: protect-ci-workflows
description: Asks a person before an agent weakens the checks that review its work. Shell guard refuses writes to .github/workflows/, .github/actions/, .github/dependabot.y*ml (redirect, rm/mv/tee/sed -i, cp into, git checkout/restore, cmdlets); reads and `chock sync` pass. Edit/Write: tool_use gate asks a person before a write to CI, hook or bot config (GitLab, Jenkins, CircleCI, CODEOWNERS, husky, more). Not judged: deletions, empty writes, shell writes to non-GitHub CI paths; plugin installs ship no gate. [Shell guard: Session-enforced in Cursor by a beforeShellExecution hook: a matched command is denied before it runs (witnessed blocking on Cursor, 2026-08-24). The hook needs git, a Python 3.11+ (python3, python or py; the Windows Store stub is skipped) and a usable bash resolved from PATH. The hook entry sets `failClosed`, which Cursor's hooks documentation (cursor.com/docs/agent/hooks) says blocks the action when the hook fails to run, so a hook that cannot start refuses the command. If the guard itself crashes, the hook returns `permission: "ask"`, which beforeShellExecution honours. Repo-wide enforcement at commit time and in CI still needs `chock sync`. Write gate: Session-enforced via PreToolUse and Stop hooks; needs git and a Python 3.11+. PreToolUse judges the file a tool call would write; Stop re-reads what the turn actually left on disk, so a file written through a shell heredoc is judged too. With no working Python the hook exits 2; without git, fail-open clients allow silently. A gate that cannot reach a decision refuses rather than allowing one it never judged. Enforcement at every commit and in CI still needs chock installed in the repo. In Cursor the turn's end is not held: a refusal there is handed back to the agent as a follow-up message, once, and a hook that fails to answer lets the turn end.]
